newsitem.title: USA: U.S. money managers stay long on US debt -- survey.
newsitem.headline: U.S. money managers stay long on US debt -- survey.

text.p: U.S. fixed-income managers remained long on U.S. debt last week and bought further out the yield curve, according to an MCM MoneyWatch Inc survey.

Money managers were "staying long (and) not finding many reasons to sell," said MCM money market analyst Peter McTeague, who conducts the asset allocation survey. They were "still bullish and a better buyer out the yield curve in recent weeks," he said.
The weekly survey showed durations as a percentage of benchmark rose to 108.2 percent in the week ended December 2 from 108.1 percent in the prior week.
A duration reading above 100 percent indicates the group of investors polled is mostly long on the market.
A portfolio's duration represents its average maturity and is used by portfolio managers to calculate exposure to risk.
In the "next likely move" category, portfolio managers representing 14 percent of total assets in the survey said they would "buy," down from 21 percent the prior week.
Strategists leaning toward "sell" rose to 35 percent, up from 32 percent in the week ended November 25.
Fifty-one percent of managers said they were "neutral" on the market, up from 47 percent a week ago.
Cash as a percentage of assets fell to 2.11 percent, against 2.20 percent registered the previous week.

The survey showed 29 percent of investors polled overweighted the 10-plus years duration sector, up from 26 percent the previous week, while 17 percent underweighted it. The remaining 54 percent were "neutral."
In the five- to 10-year duration sector, 44 percent of investors polled said they overweighted the securities and 7.0 percent underweighted them.
The survey included 40 domestic participants, who manage about $100 billion in fixed-income assets. The poll is conducted weekly by MCM and usually is released on Tuesday.
